content:
It seems to me that, when defining sets, we sometimes add a space after the opening brace and before the closing one, see for instance
{ f x y | (x : X) (y : Y) } is notation for the set of elements f x y constructed from the
But sometimes we don't, as in
https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2fb84f40125bfc66936eff5dea70c236315f17b2/Mathlib/Data/Set/Defs.lean#L157

(yes, the second line is extracted from the same comment as the first).

I think we should set a standard and document it here
https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/style.html

Preferences?
In paper maths there is no space, so that's my preference

As a general PSA, in the near future the FRO will release a code formatter which will automatically settle many of these debates.

So personally I think that for matters where we've managed to live without a clear consensus for several years now, we would do best to leave the decision to that code formatter. Otherwise we risk a lot of unnecessary bikeshedding and code churn.
My own preference for this issue is to have no spaces except for Subtype, i.e. { p : Fin 8 × Fin 8 // p.1 + p.2 = 3 }

Johan Commelin said:

As a general PSA, in the near future the FRO will release a code formatter which will automatically settle many of these debates.

Sure but decisions of this code formatter will come from somewhere. In this particular case, if Leo doesn’t have a clear opinion and Mathlib decides something then I think it will become the code formatter opinion.
The good thing in that case is the answer is clear: spaces after an opening brace of before a closing one are simply ugly and nowhere seen on paper.

Patrick Massot said:

Sure but decisions of this code formatter will come from somewhere.

In particular, the notation in question is not provided by core, so it seems unlikely that it would be able to declare a preferred style.
I believe most spaces in that notation were automatically added during the port cause that's what the pretty printer happened to be using

Yaël Dillies said:

In paper maths there is no space, so that's my preference

But in paper maths there is also no space around +, -, >, <, etc.
I guess it depends on what you call a space but I think there is
{12+34}\{12+34\}{12+34}

IMO there is a space after an opening brace in paper maths, which I also add in LaTeX: { x∣x∈R }\{\,x\mid x \in \mathbb{R}\,\}{x∣x∈R}
As the above shows, it's up to interpretation

Just for completeness: you're of course free to do whatever you want with your LaTeX code, but adding \, before braces is discouraged by AMS-TeX (and reverted in the copy-editing review performed by several journals)
I strongly prefer spaces inside a set builder notation and a subtype declaration.
